title: Signal catalogue cold-start sync: batch upsert local signals to GitHub Issues and back
description: Signal a1000037 (in the Ouro project) defines the ongoing event-driven flow: one signal created → one issue created; one state transition → one comment posted. That flow is intentionally lean and per-event. It has no mechanism for the cold-start case: when GitHub sync is first enabled, existing local signals have no github_issue_url and existing GitHub Issues have no moeb ingest comment. Without a batch sync command the catalogue and GitHub diverge at setup time and cannot be reconciled without manual intervention. The same gap applies after connectivity loss or a fresh clone of the repository.
proposed_resolution: Implement `moeb signal sync [--source moeb|project] [--dry-run]` as a standalone CLI command (no conductor required). The command must: (1) for each local signal without a github_issue_url, create a GitHub Issue via the API, populate the issue body and labels using the conventions defined in a1000037, and write the returned issue URL back into the signal JSON as github_issue_url; (2) for each GitHub Issue in the configured repository that carries no moeb ingest comment, create a local signal JSON in the catalogue and post the standard ingest comment; (3) for each local signal with a github_issue_url that resolves to an open issue but the signal is archived or resolved, close the issue with a resolution comment. All three passes must be idempotent — re-running sync must never create duplicate issues or signals. The command must print a summary of created, updated, and skipped entries. --dry-run must print the planned changes without writing anything.
